title: Comprehensive AI review of the delayed-feedback vertical slice

limitations: The reviewer is an AI system, not a human domain expert.
The review can analyze logic, mathematics, source metadata, wording, and internal consistency but cannot provide human professional accountability.
No empirical system was tested by this review.

matched: Chapter 4 dynamic behavior and stability scope
source_verification.scope_boundary: The textbook supports feedback, dynamic-behavior, and stability terminology. The Atlas period-six recurrence result is derived independently and is not attributed to the textbook.

mathematical_verification.proof: The deterministic second-order recurrence has the same ordered state pair at t=1 and t=7, so all later states repeat with period dividing 6. The first six states exclude periods 1, 2, and 3, establishing exact period 6.
mathematical_verification.stability_boundary: The orbit is bounded and periodic; the result is not a proof of instability.

entities.summary: The question is bounded to a discrete scalar recurrence and explicitly asks for inference limits.
Bibliographic metadata and relevant chapter scope match the authoritative Caltech repository; the source-use boundary is explicit.
The generated-analysis source has a declared procedure and is correctly separated from empirical evidence.
The sequence is correct and now includes an exact ordered-state proof of period 6.
The claim is now precise: exact bounded period-six orbit for one recurrence, parameter set, and initial history.
The model-to-world inference boundary is correct and prevents formal output from being treated as empirical identification.
The definition is broad enough for cross-domain use while its boundaries prevent transfer of parameters or interventions by analogy alone.
The concept distinguishes recurrence periodicity from measured physical oscillation and does not equate an oscillatory solution with instability.
The model now states its initial-history requirement, exact period proof, assumptions, and non-transferable failure modes.
The synthesis accurately combines the formal period-six result with a strict model-adequacy boundary and no instability overclaim.

findings.summary: Eight displayed states were insufficient by themselves to prove indefinite periodicity.
findings.resolution: Revisions 2 of the model, evidence, claim, and synthesis now prove return of the deterministic ordered state pair after six steps and exclude smaller divisor periods.

findings.summary: The slice needed to state that a bounded periodic orbit is not automatically unstable.
findings.resolution: Revisions 2 explicitly describe a bounded period-six orbit and separate oscillation from instability.

findings.summary: The authoritative source supported general terminology but did not analyze the exact Atlas recurrence.
findings.resolution: Source revision 2 and synthesis revision 2 now state that the recurrence proof is independently derived.
